meta.scene_summary: We are busy building the future with AI while the rest of our infrastructure is held together by hope and duct tape.

cooking.headline: Turns out AI agents are better at bank robbery than entry-level employees
cooking.summary: South Korean officials suspect AI agents were deployed to hack into banks, essentially automating the most high-stakes heist in history. It is truly the ultimate group project where the AI does all the heavy lifting while the human just sits back and watches the results.
cooking.plain_english: South Korean authorities have identified evidence suggesting that automated artificial intelligence systems were used to conduct cyberattacks against the nation's financial institutions.

cooking.headline: GPT-6 is here to automate the parts of your job you were actually getting paid for
cooking.summary: OpenAI just dropped GPT-6 with a new UI that promises to handle your workflow, effectively turning your browser into a self-driving car. It is the perfect tool for when you want to feel productive while watching an AI hallucinate your entire sprint backlog.
cooking.plain_english: OpenAI has released GPT-6, which includes new features designed to help users manage and interact with various software applications.

cooking.headline: Claude Haiku 5.5 is here to prove that 'small model' is just marketing speak for 'cheap and fast'.
cooking.summary: Anthropic dropped a new version of their smallest model, because apparently, the industry decided that being tiny is now a competitive advantage. It's the perfect tool for when you need a hallucination delivered in under 200 milliseconds.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic has released a new, more efficient version of its smaller artificial intelligence model.

cooking.headline: OpenSSH 10.6 is here to remind you that your server security is still held together by duct tape.
cooking.summary: Another OpenSSH update has arrived, which means it is time to log into your servers and hope your config files do not immediately combust. It is the digital version of a routine maintenance check that you secretly hope does not reveal that the foundation of your house is rotting.
cooking.plain_english: The OpenSSH project has released version 10.6, which includes updates and security improvements for the software used to remotely manage servers.

cooking.headline: Chemistry Nobel winners prove that sometimes the best results come from just letting molecules do their thing.
cooking.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai just took home the Nobel for work that essentially makes chemistry less like a messy kitchen and more like a precise assembly line.

cooked.headline: The internet's digital ID system just got its lunch money stolen
cooked.summary: Hackers managed to grab counterfeit TLS certificates for major services like Google, proving that even our most trusted locks are just suggestions. It is the digital equivalent of someone printing their own master key and walking right into your house.
cooked.plain_english: Unauthorized individuals successfully obtained fake digital security certificates that allow them to impersonate major websites like Google.

cooked.headline: Media conglomerates are merging to form a final boss that nobody asked for
cooked.summary: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery just pulled a $111 billion mega-merger to create a single giant streaming monolith.

cooked.headline: GitHub went down, and suddenly everyone remembered they don't actually know how to code without pulling.
cooked.summary: GitHub had an incident with Git operations today, effectively forcing the entire industry to take an unexpected coffee break. It's a great reminder that the cloud is just someone else's computer, and today, that computer was busy thinking about its life choices.
cooked.plain_english: GitHub experienced a service outage that temporarily prevented users from performing standard version control operations.

cooked.headline: Visa and Mastercard are being sued for fees that basically act as a toll booth for the entire internet.
cooked.summary: It turns out that taking a percentage of every single transaction for decades has finally triggered a massive legal headache. It is the corporate equivalent of charging your friends a convenience fee every time they pay you back for pizza.
cooked.plain_english: Visa, Mastercard, and several major banks are being sued for allegedly setting credit card transaction fees at artificially high levels.

cooked.headline: Sony's security is currently playing a game of whack-a-mole with a hammer made of glass.
cooked.summary: PS5 jailbreaks are moving so fast that Sony's security team is effectively trying to patch a leaky boat with a single roll of duct tape. It turns out that when you treat hardware like a locked vault, people just get better at picking the lock.
cooked.plain_english: Security researchers are successfully bypassing the software restrictions on the PlayStation 5 at an increasing rate.
